The edit broke the file — `$'
'` was interpolated literally and inserted a newline plus a stray `
'` line. Rewriting the file correctly:The line is now `IFS=$'
'`, and all other lines are untouched.

One note on behavior: with `read -r` on a here-string, newline is not actually a valid word separator — it delimits lines, so only the first line becomes a field. The test `$'a
b
c'` printed only `[a]`. Since you asked to change only that line, I left the rest as is; if you want split-on-newlines behavior, `read`/`IFS` won't do it — a `mapfile`/`while IFS= read -r` loop over the argument would be needed.
